gen-silkscreen-gf-biz-udpgothic: Silkscreen spaces every letter apart so widely you can nearly feel the gaps, its lines laid out like spaghetti. BIZ UDPGothic keeps its own lavish spacing, so round letters feel welcoming.
gen-silkscreen-gf-bpmf-zihi-kai-std: Lo-fi and retro: Silkscreen scatters spaced-out letters like spaghetti, while Bpmf Zihi Kai Std draws a restrained swell. Reading it would feel smooth, its counters staying open to the outside.
gen-silkscreen-gf-cairo: Cairo opens a wide channel into every bowl, while Silkscreen spaces its lettering out like loose spaghetti. Only the heading keeps its curves fully thick through every turn.
gen-silkscreen-gf-elms-sans: Silkscreen leaves space around every letter you can almost feel. Elms Sans draws a ballpoint-like line of constant weight, with a see-through gap in each s, so the two sit together easily.
gen-silkscreen-gf-encode-sans-sc: Silkscreen lets each letter float in its own space, strung out like spaghetti. Encode Sans SC brings shallow terminal curls and wide gaps, supplying the sturdy, grounded quality the heading lacks.
gen-silkscreen-gf-encode-sans-semi-expan: Retro through and through, Silkscreen strings its letters out with space you can almost feel. And Encode Sans Semi Expanded, a sans-serif of rounded, open letters, gives it a contemporary counterweight.
gen-silkscreen-gf-exo: Exo keeps wide gaps that hold tiny sizes crisp, a steady partner for Silkscreen and its spaghetti spacing. The heading's bowls and stems share one weight, its best trait.
gen-silkscreen-gf-exo-2: Silkscreen spaces its letters out, with diagonals that match its stems. Exo 2 does the opposite job, giving curves plenty of daylight inside so text stays clear while the heading plays.
gen-silkscreen-gf-finlandica: Lo-fi spaghetti, in letters: Silkscreen spaces each one out until you can almost feel the gaps. Finlandica brings open-mouthed e crossbars and a constant-width outline you can follow with a finger.
gen-silkscreen-gf-google-sans: Silkscreen puts space around every letter you can almost feel, strung out like lo-fi spaghetti. And Google Sans works alongside it with no thick-thin shift and terminals pulled well back, so text stays approachable.
